Sample.Title: control_rep1

Channel.Characteristics: Lymphoblastoid cell line derived from peripheral blood mononuclear cells
Channel.Extract-Protocol: Total RNA was isolated from LCL using the TRIzol (Invitrogen) isolation method according to the manufacturer’s protocols.
Channel.Label: Cy3
Channel.Label-Protocol: 10 ug of total RNA were primed with 2 ul of Random Hexamer Primers (3 mg/mL) at 70°C for 10 min, then reversed transcribed at 42°C overnight in the presence of 400 U SuperScript II RTase (Invitrogen), and 1.2 ul of 25X aminoallyl-dNTP mix (Ambion). 4.5 ul of the appropriate NHS-ester Cy dye (AmershamPharmacia) in DMSO was added to aa-cDNA.

Channel.Extract-Protocol: Total RNA was isolated from LCL using the TRIzol (Invitrogen) isolation method according to the manufacturer’s protocols.
Channel.Label: Cy5
Channel.Label-Protocol: 10 ug of total RNA were primed with 2 ul of Random Hexamer Primers (3 mg/mL) at 70°C for 10 min, then reversed transcribed at 42°C overnight in the presence of 400 U SuperScript II RTase (Invitrogen), and 1.2 ul of 25X aminoallyl-dNTP mix (Ambion). 4.5 ul of the appropriate NHS-ester Cy dye (AmershamPharmacia) in DMSO was added to aa-cDNA.

Sample.Hybridization-Protocol: The two differentially labeled probes (Cy3 vs Cy5) were mixed and dried. 1X hybridization buffer (50% formamide, 5X SSC, and 0.1% SDS), as well as Human COT1-DNA (Life Technologies) and Poly(A)-DNA (Pharmacia) were added. Each sample was hybridized on a TIGR40K cDNA microarray overnight. After hybridization, slides were washed sequentially.
Sample.Scan-Protocol: Scanned on an GenePix 4000B scanner. Images were quantified using TIGR Spotfinder.
Sample.Data-Processing: The intensity data was normalized and filtered using Lowess normalization and standard deviation regularization within Midas software and analyzed using MeV, which are open-access software programs for DNA microarray analyses. All analyses were performed with a 70% data filter which means that each gene included in the analyses must have an expression value in 70% of the 116 samples studied. Significant differentially expressed genes were identified using the Significance Analysis of Microarrays (SAM) module within MeV for both 2-class and 4-class analyses, with a maximum false discovery rate (FDR) of 5%.

Series.Title: Gene expression profiling differentiates autism case-controls and phenotypic variants of autism spectrum disorders
Series.Summary: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by delayed/abnormal language development, deficits in social interaction, repetitive behaviors and restricted interests. The heterogeneity in clinical presentation of ASD, likely due to different etiologies, complicates genetic/biological analyses of these disorders. DNA microarray analyses were conducted on 116 lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL) from individuals with idiopathic autism who are divided into 3 phenotypic subgroups according to severity scores from the commonly used Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised questionnaire and age-matched, nonautistic controls. Statistical analyses of gene expression data from control LCL against that of LCL from ASD probands identify genes for which expression levels are either quantitatively or qualitatively associated with phenotypic severity. Comparison of the significant differentially expressed genes from each subgroup relative to the control group reveals differentially expressed genes unique to each subgroup as well as genes in common across subgroups. Among the findings unique to the most severely affected ASD group are genes that regulate circadian rhythm, which has been shown to have multiple effects on neurological as well as metabolic functions commonly dysregulated in autism. Among the genes common to all 3 subgroups of ASD are 5 novel genes which appear to associate with androgen sensitivity, which may underlie the strong 4:1 bias towards affected males.
Series.Overall-Design: Gene expression profiling of 116 LCL from autistic (87) and nonautistic (29) individuals were obtained using a custom-printed DNA microarray containing 39,936 elements (TIGR 40K Human array, GPL3427) and a reference design in which each sample was compared to the Stratagene Universal Human RNA standard. The 87 autistic samples were divided into phenotypic subgroups (language, mild, savant) on the basis of cluster analyses of scores from an autism diagnostic questionnaire, the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised instrument. Differentially expressed genes were determined for all autistic vs. control groups, as well as for each of 3 phenotypic ASD groups and controls.
